ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure is a triangular coordinate graph, the three axes are respectively labeled a, b, and c, and use 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, and 100% as scales. The four points are respectively Jia, Yi, Bing, and Ding. Jia is located in the lower-left part of the triangle, Yi is located in the lower-right part, Bing is located in the upper middle part, and Ding is located near the top. According to the meaning of the question, a, b, and c respectively represent the output-value proportions of the primary industry, secondary industry, and tertiary industry. Estimated from the positions in the figure, Jia has a relatively high primary-industry proportion, a certain proportion of secondary industry, and a relatively low tertiary industry; Bing has a relatively high tertiary-industry proportion and a relatively high level of industrial structure.
Then reason: Industrial transfer usually moves from regions with relatively developed economies, a need to upgrade industrial structure, and relatively high labor costs, toward regions with relatively underdeveloped economies, lower labor costs, and a certain industrial receiving foundation. Among the four countries, Bing's industrial structure is more advanced and it is most likely the industrial transfer-out place; Jia is relatively backward but has a certain secondary-industry foundation, so it is relatively suitable as an industrial receiving place. Therefore the most likely industrial transfer direction is from Bing to Jia.
